$comment: The capability vocabulary (platform plan 3.2): one list, used by nodes, packages, and integrations alike. A package's manifest.requires/optional and a Device's capabilities both draw from this list. Not to be confused with the robot's 20-item capability GRANT list (3.1), which is a later (Hub v0.3 / robot authorization) addition, out of spec v0.1 scope. The engine roles (vision, image, video, music, stt, tts) are named exactly as the Stack's role ids so a manifest's requires and the hub's engine allocation share one list; the chat role maps to gpu_llm or cpu_llm and the embed role to embeddings (home/docs/plans/hardware-tiers-2026-09-23.md, Capabilities follow the allocation). Robot part and verb names live in vocab/robot-api.json; this list owns every capability id that robot profiles declare. Existing robot body ids include head_6dof (head with six degrees of freedom), head_pan_tilt (head that pans and tilts only), roll (head roll), antennas (movable antennas), body_yaw (body rotation about the vertical axis), eyes (display or actuated eyes), mouth (display or actuated mouth), light_ring (addressable light ring), doa (direction-of-arrival from the mic array), state_feed (live joint and sensor state stream), encoders (joint position encoders), touch (touch sensing), distance (distance sensing), imu (inertial measurement unit), battery_readout (reports battery level), physical_mute (hardware mute switch), camera_shutter (physical camera shutter), moves_recorded (plays prerecorded moves), speech_pod (speech is placed on the pod), speech_robot (speech is placed on the robot itself). Robot object ids add connection (a live body link), power (power and wake lifecycle), estop (emergency stop control), lease (exclusive motion control), appendages (named movable parts), base (mobile movement), posture (body stance), dock (charger seeking), health (part status), pose (position and heading), network (link details), system (identity and resources), log (bounded event records), and diagnostics (available checks). New observation capabilities: gestures (closed hand-gesture observations) and sound_events (closed on-body audio-event labels; vocabulary only, processing remains disabled until separately scheduled). The robot capability no_vendor_login means the body has no published login password to change; Home skips its password-rotation gate for a robot declaring it.
